questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Albania?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Albania article.

questions.proof: The capital is Tirana, and other important cities are Durrës, Elbasan and Vlora.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Albania?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Albania on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Geography” part of the Albania article.

questions.proof: Albania is bordered by Greece, the Republic of North Macedonia, Montenegro and Kosovo.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Albania?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Albania article.

questions.proof: The official language is Albanian (Gjuha Shqipe).

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Albania is next to Montenegro, _____, North Macedonia, Kosovo and Greece.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “Montenegro”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Albania article.

questions.proof: Albania is next to Montenegro, Serbia, North Macedonia, Kosovo and Greece.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “The Albanian Armed Forces were first formed after independence in _____.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twentieth century.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Armed forces” part of the Albania article.

questions.proof: The Albanian Armed Forces were first formed after independence in 1912.
